text:
Which among the following will be the major product of the given reaction?


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The substrate is 4,7-dioxooctanoic acid, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}$ (C-1 is the carboxyl carbon), a 1,4-diketone; in 10% $\mathrm{KOH}$ the acid is present as its carboxylate and the two ketone groups undergo intramolecular aldol condensation to a five-membered ring.

Two five-membered closures are possible: the C-8 methyl enolate adding to the C-4 carbonyl, or the C-3 methylene enolate adding to the C-7 methyl-ketone carbonyl. The aldol additions are reversible, and the dehydration step favours the more substituted, more stable conjugated alkene, so the C-3 to C-7 closure gives the major product (the route by which undecane-2,5-dione gives dihydrojasmone, 3-methyl-2-pentylcyclopent-2-en-1-one).

Ring closure of C-3 onto C-7 and loss of water give a cyclopent-2-en-1-one carrying $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ on C-3 and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COO}{}^{-}$ on C-2, with a tetrasubstituted $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$; acidification with $\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{+}$ gives 2-(carboxymethyl)-3-methylcyclopent-2-en-1-one.

The other closure gives only the trisubstituted 3-(2-carboxyethyl)cyclopent-2-en-1-one, and a six-membered ring would need an enolate next to the carboxylate group, which does not form.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text:
In the following brown complex, the oxidation state of iron is $+_____________$.

$[Fe(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+}+NO\to [Fe(H_{2}O)_{5}(NO)]^{2+}_{\text{Brown complex}}+H_{2}O$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the oxidation state of iron in the brown complex $[Fe(H_{2}O)_{5}(NO)]^{2+}$, we need to analyze the ligands and their charges, as well as the overall charge of the complex.

Step 1: Understanding the Complex
The complex is:

$[Fe(H_{2}O)_{5}(NO)]^{2+}$

Iron (Fe): The central metal atom whose oxidation state we need to find.

Ligands:

5 Water Molecules ($H_{2}O$): Neutral ligands (charge = 0).

1 Nitrosyl Group (NO): Can have different charges depending on its mode of bonding.

Step 2: Assigning Charges to Ligands

Water ($H_{2}O$): Neutral ligand, so it contributes 0 to the overall charge.

Nitrosyl (NO): Can act as:

NO${}^{+}$ (nitrosonium ion) with a +1 charge.

NO (neutral molecule) with 0 charge.

NO${}^{-}$ (nitroxide ion) with a –1 charge.

Step 3: Setting Up the Oxidation State Equation
Let $x$ be the oxidation state of Fe.

The sum of the oxidation states of all components equals the overall charge of the complex:

$x+(5\times 0)+(\text{Charge of NO})=+2$

Simplifying:

$x+(\text{Charge of NO})=+2$

Step 4: Determining the Charge of NO in the Complex
In the brown ring complex, experimental evidence shows that the nitrosyl ligand acts as NO${}^{+}$. This is because:

The NO ligand forms a linear bond with Fe, characteristic of NO${}^{+}$.

The complex is known to involve a reduction of the oxidation state of Fe to an unusual value.

Thus, Charge of NO = +1.

Step 5: Calculating the Oxidation State of Fe
Substitute the charge of NO into the equation:

$x+(+1)=+2$

Solving for $x$:

$x=+2-(+1)=+1$

Therefore, the oxidation state of Fe in the brown complex is $+1$.

Conclusion
The oxidation state of iron in $[Fe(H_{2}O)_{5}(NO)]^{2+}$ is +1.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift
